body:
Pass 19. Epic 6 verified. Suite 1733 pass / 0 fail on the current tree.

Prepared the Epic 7 reference while you were between epics. Training-only vs all-runs Sigma, 500 reps, null data: paired difference z = +0.29 / +0.83 / +0.19 at shrinkage 0 / 0.05 / 0.2. NO detectable leakage - the theoretically expected answer, since GLM residuals are exactly orthogonal to the fitted betas.

The design point: Epic 7 is an EQUIVALENCE study, not a difference study. "No significant difference" is a power statement, not a leakage statement. State an equivalence margin up front and size the replications to it - at 500 reps the paired se is ~1e-4, certifying equivalence to about 3e-4.

Scope caveat worth putting in the result: my simulation satisfies the Gaussian linear model exactly, which is what makes orthogonality hold. The real risks are misspecified design, autocorrelation estimated from the same data, or a structured shrinkage target. Consider running one misspecified arm too - otherwise the epic certifies equivalence only under the conditions that guarantee it.

Full numbers in the decision note on the bead.
